target.title: fix(macos): read shell-first launchd auth env
target.body:
Related: #98589
Supersedes/combines the relevant macOS LaunchAgent env-wrapper coverage from #98697 and #99889.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users running the local gateway from a generated LaunchAgent env wrapper could see GUI/local gateway auth fail when `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` or `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` existed only in the generated LaunchAgent env file.

This also covers the newer shell-first LaunchAgent shape where `ProgramArguments` starts with `/bin/sh`, then the generated wrapper path, then the generated env file path before the actual `openclaw gateway ...` command.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Swift LaunchAgent snapshot parser now mirrors the Node launchd env-wrapper contract: it only reads generated env files when the wrapper and env file are sibling files under `service-env`, with matching `<label>-env-wrapper.sh` and `<label>.env` names. It unwraps both direct wrapper and shell-first wrapper arguments so downstream macOS gateway status/auth code sees the real gateway command and file-backed auth values.

The custom-wrapper case remains intentionally untouched so arbitrary `*-env-wrapper.sh` command lines are not overmatched.

## User Impact

macOS GUI/local gateway auth can use the same file-backed LaunchAgent token/password that the generated gateway service uses, including the shell-first wrapper layout on current main. Custom wrapper LaunchAgents keep their original arguments and are not treated as OpenClaw-generated env wrappers unless they match the generated `service-env` contract.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check`
- Added Swift tests for:
  - generated `service-env/<label>-env-wrapper.sh` + `<label>.env` parsing
  - shell-first `/bin/sh <wrapper> <env> openclaw gateway ...` parsing
  - custom wrapper arguments staying untouched

Not run locally:

- macOS Swift tests / SwiftFormat, because this development machine is Windows and does not have `swift` or `swiftformat` available. The PR relies on GitHub macOS CI for that lane.

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change: the parser accepts only OpenClaw-generated LaunchAgent env-wrapper layouts, merges generated env-file auth over inline plist env, unwraps the generated wrapper command before extracting gateway flags, and preserves custom wrapper commands.
